title: Generative agents built from interview transcripts simulate 1,000 people
summary: LLM agents built from participants' full interview transcripts reproduced their General Social Survey answers at about 85% of the rate at which participants reproduced their own answers two weeks later, a normalized score. They also matched personality and economic-game results (normalized correlations of about 0.80 and 0.66) and replicated four of five behavioural experiments. Caveat: arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, and the results are normalized rather than raw accuracy.
ai_technology: Generative agent architecture with LLM and full interview transcripts
organization: Stanford University; Google DeepMind; Northwestern University; University of Washington

evidence.tested: Agents built from interview and survey data of 1,052 Americans were scored on held-out General Social Survey items against participants' own two-week test-retest consistency, and on personality, economic-game and experiment replications.
evidence.unknown: Preprint, not peer reviewed; there is no dedicated limitations section, and combining interviews and surveys gave only modest gains over either source.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM was the engine of agents that answer questions on behalf of individuals, grounded in their self-report data.
